 1(b) Dhayanandha,

 SCCH-23 3 MVC-1535/2021  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 11.06.2020 at about 7.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-JQ-5889 and proceeding along with pillion rider by name Mr. Siddaraju and petitioner was driving the same in slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of NH- 206 road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When he reached near Bommanahalli Gate, NH-206 road, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumkur District, at that time driver of Tractor - Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-44-TA-3025 and KA-44-TA-3024 drove the same in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life came from opposite side i.e.,
from Tiptur side came to the extreme right side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.

As a result of which he and rider of the motorcycle sustained grievous injuries and after the accident he was shifted to Tiptur Government Hospital, for first aid treatement, then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has taken OPD treatment at K.C. General Hospital, Bengaluru and thereby he has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, at the time of accident he was working as driver and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.

It is further Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
2 urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor and Trailer.

The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer, the respondent No.1(a) & (b) are the LR's of deceased respondent No.1 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Respondent No.11(a) and (b) being the LR's of deceased respondent No.1.
They are not appeared before this tribunal.
Hence they placed exparte.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tractor - Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA- 44-TA-3025 and KA-44-TA-3024.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

It is contended in MVC.141/2023 that the alleged accident occurred at the night time and unknown car hit to the petitioner's scooter and run away from the spot or the rider of the scooter himself hit to the unknown car, hence scooter is the true vehicle involved in the accident and not the alleged insured tractor and trailer.

It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of one day in lodging the complaint that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the insurance company.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a Road Traffic accident on 11.06.2020 at about 7.30 p.m, near Bommenahalli Gate, NH-206 road, Kasaba Hobli,
tiptur Taluk, Tumkur district and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tractor - Trailer bearing No.KA-44-TA-3025 &
KA-44-TA-3024 ?

Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
3
2) Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?

If so from whom and to what extent?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 20 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy was examined as PW.2.
Ex.P.21 to 24 were marked through him.
Ex. P.11(a) was marked by way of confrontation during the course of cross-examination of PW.1.
The petitioner has also examined the eye-witness / Siddaraju (petitioner in MVC.141/2023) as PW.3.
Ex. P.25
and 26 were marked through him.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has examined the Casuality Medical Officer of Tiptur Government Hospital as RW.1.
Ex.R.1 & 2 were marked through him.
Further the Manager - Legal of respondent No.2 insurance company has examined as RW.2 and through him got marked Ex.R.4 & 5 documents.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: The evidence of PW.1 and police documents indicate that on 11.06.2020 an the accident had taken place and on 12.06.2020 a complaint was lodged against the driver of unknown Swaraj Tractor.
Based on the complaint, police registered the FIR and took up investigation.
During the course of investigation, material evidence connected to the accident was collected by the Investigating Officer.

The history of the injuries mentioned in (police intimation which is marked as document at Ex.P.19 in MVC.141/2023) and the wound certificate (Ex.P.7) establishes that the clamant (Rajashekar) was rider and (Siddaraju - in MVC.141/20213) who was proceeding as pillion rider have sustained injuries in a Road Traffic Accident.
No doubt in these documents at the first instance the type of the vehicle is mentioned as 'car' and later made correction as strike out / over written by Tractor.
But the vehicle number is not mentioned and only the type of vehicle is written.
But having regard to the need of the hour i.e., giving immediate medical attention to the victims which would be a priority at that time, these documents cannot be expected to be an encyclopedia.
Even otherwise for the lapse on the part of the hospital authorities, the victim / petitioners cannot be punished.
Moreso, when the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident in question is evident from the other documents placed on record.

10. The learned counsel for the Insurance Company laid emphasis on the entry made in the history column of Ex.P.19 / Ex.R.1 & 2 wherein it is mentioned that 'H/o RTA hit by a car while going in a bike" and vociferously argued that in the place of 'car' it is manipulated as 'tractor' and thereby prayed to dismiss the petition.

But the fact that deserves notice is that in Ex.R.3/police intimation,
Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
4
in the column the injured persons name is clearly mentioned and also clearly mentioned the date and time also.
Generally, not only the victim but also the person who brings him to the hospital would be in trauma.
The possibility of providing improper information at such time cannot be ruled out.

Moreover due to rush of work and constant pressure under which the hospital authorities work,
there might have been some discrepancies in recording the details at the said column.
This entry alone thus cannot be the basis to conclude that the petitioner sustained injuries on account of car but not from Tractor.
11. Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested both the vehicles and found that their brake systems were in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles.
Therefore the driver of the tractor did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle.

Such being the case, the very fact that he dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle in a rash &
negligent manner.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer to displace the version of the accident as deposed by the injured claimant.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor - Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-44-TA-3025 and KA-44-TA-3024.
12.

The other discrepancy that the insurance company is banking upon is the date of occurrence of accident which in the history of injuries column of MLC Extract of the petitioner from Government Hospital, Tiptur is mentioned as car and later made correction as strike out / over written by Tractor.

But the author of this document i.e., Dr. Vijaykumar of the Government Hospital, Tiptur who was examined as RW.1 by insurance company candidly admitted that they have came to our hospital earlier themselves, have stated that the alleged H/o RTA was hit by Car and later on told that hit by Tractor and hence he has made correction as strike out / over written in MLC book.
The learned counsel for petitioner could not elicit anything worthwhile to negate his testimony.

13. During the arguments the learned advocate for insurance company argued that in the discharge summary Ex.P.11 the doctor was mentioned as alleged history of RTA on 11.06.2020 at around 6.30 p.m near Tiptur on Tiptur - Shivamogga road when patient was driving 2-wheeler and skid and fell down trying to avoid a dog which came in between and sustained injujry to right lower limb and right upper limb.
Therefore it creats doubts hence he prayed to reject the petition.
14. It is relevant to note that in Ex.P.11 the treated doctor mentioned the above said lines.
The petitioner examined him as PW.2.
The advocate for respondent No.2 fully cross-examined the PW.2.
But in the cross-examination the learned advocate for respondent No.2 not raised the above question.

As already discussed, the petitioner after the accident first visited to Govt. Hospital,
Tiptur, wherein MLC was recorded as hit by car, thereafter it was rectified as a Tractor and very next day FIR was registered.

If the petitioner fell down try to avoid the dog it must be reflected in MLC of Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
5 Tiptur Hospital.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It seems that at the issuance of discharge summary Ex.P.11 officials of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital made a mistake by copy paste in the computer.
Therefore, the learned advocate for respondent No.2 not raised regarding the same during the cross-examination of PW.2.

Therefore,
the question raised during the argument cannot be considerable.
15. The petitioner's father herein lodged the complaint and thereby set the criminal law into motion.
It is true that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.
But under the circumstances when the petitioner was severely injured he was not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the complaint with the police.

Even otherwise, when the injured was admitted to the hospital for taking treatment due to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, it was the bounden duty of the hospital authorities to send the MLC intimation to the concerned police station, who were duty bound to rush to the hospital, record the statement of the injured and register the case at the earliest.
For their fault petitioner cannot be blamed.
Such being the case, merely because complaint was not lodged on the very same day is not a ground to suspect the occurrence of the accident and the injuries suffered by the petitioner therefrom.

In any case as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Omprakash V/s Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2017) 1 SCC 724, delay in intimation of the accident or submission of the documents due to unavoidable circumstances, should not bar settlement of a genuine case.

entities.text: Omprakash V/s Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2017) 1 SCC 724
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered in the 'Affirmative'.
17. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Tractor & trailer.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
18. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has exhibited his Driving Liceence & PAN Card at Ex.P12 & 13, wherein his date of birth is reflected as 12.04.1990.
This indicates that he was aged 30 years on the date of accident.
19. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was working as Driver and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.

The Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
6
notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 11.06.2020.
Therefore, Rs.14,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

20. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Lacerated wound of 20x10x15 cm over anteromedial aspect of right leg exposing the fracture bones, muscles with severe organic contamination, swelling of right leg present, deformity present, lacerated wound of 2x3 cms over right forearm extensor aspect.
It is needless to say that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The discharge summary of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital (Ex.P.11) indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 12.06.2020 to 10.07.2020 (29 days in total).

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : 1) Wound debridement ND Ex-Fix for both bone leg K-Wire for medial malleoli, distal radius, metacarpal and phalanx fracture done on 20.06.2020 under SAB,
2) ORIF with plate and screw for forearm and wound debridement for right leg done on 29.06.2020 under BPB.
21.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has restricted ROM in right knee and ankle, right hand, wrist, and elbow, along with pain in right leg, ankle, wrist and elbow, along with pain in right leg, ankle, wrist, elbow and hand.
He has 27% whole body disability due to permanent physical impairment in right lower limb.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 9%.
22.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 29 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.750/- per day and a sum of Rs.21,750/- (750 X 29) is awarded under this head.

Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
7 23. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.58,000/- (14,500 X 4) under this head.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P8, the petitioner has spent Rs.3,93,020/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross- examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,93,020/- which is rounded off to Rs.3,93,000/- towards medical expenses.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,66,220/- (Rs.14,500 X 12 X 17 X 9/100) which is rounded off to Rs.2,66,200/- is awarded under this head.
27. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
28. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.15,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.
29. The calculation table stands as follows :

1 Attendant charges, extra : 21,750-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 40,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 58,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 3,93,000-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 2,66,200-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7

Future medical expenses :
15,000-00 Total 8,43,950-00 30.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

Rajashekar B.R vs Mahalingaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23906320/
8 31.
The contention taken up by the respondent No.2 that the petitioner / rider of the vehicle was under the influence of alcohol /intoxication stated and that has contributed for the accident.
In order to substantiate the above said contention, apart from self serving and self proclaimed statement of respondent No.2 there is absolutely no materials placed before this court.
Added more in Ex.P.9 charge sheet there is absolutely nothing has been whispered by the IO.
The IO has also not invoked Sec.185 of MV Act.
Moreover during the course of cross-examination of RW.2 he has also categorically admitted that there are no documents produced that the rider of the vehicle was in intoxicated state.
Hence the contentions urged by the respondent No.2 does not hold any water in the eye of law.
32. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner, he died during the pendency and respondent No.1(a) and (b) being the LR's of deceased respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Tractor - Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-44-TA-3025 and KA-44-TA- 3024 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
33. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,43,950/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/ RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Per contra it is alleged that the rider of motorcycle who was riding the said vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Generally, not only the victim but also the person who brings him to the hospital would be in trauma.
The possibility of providing improper information at such time cannot be ruled out.
This entry alone thus cannot be the basis to conclude that the petitioner sustained injuries on account of car but not from Tractor.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles.
Therefore the driver of the tractor did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle.
Such being the case, the very fact that he dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle in a rash &
negligent manner.
It is true that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.
But under the circumstances when the petitioner was severely injured he was not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the complaint with the police.
Even otherwise, when the injured was admitted to the hospital for taking treatment due to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, it was the bounden duty of the hospital authorities to send the MLC intimation to the concerned police station, who were duty bound to rush to the hospital, record the statement of the injured and register the case at the earliest.
For their fault petitioner cannot be blamed.
Such being the case, merely because complaint was not lodged on the very same day is not a ground to suspect the occurrence of the accident and the injuries suffered by the petitioner therefrom.
In any case as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Omprakash V/s Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2017) 1 SCC 724, delay in intimation of the accident or submission of the documents due to unavoidable circumstances, should not bar settlement of a genuine case.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a Road Traffic accident on 11.06.2020 at about 7.30 p.m, near Bommenahalli Gate, NH-206 road, Kasaba Hobli,
tiptur Taluk, Tumkur district and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tractor - Trailer bearing No.KA-44-TA-3025 &
KA-44-TA-3024 ?
2) Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?
If so from whom and to what extent?
3) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer to displace the version of the accident as deposed by the injured claimant.
16. In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore, Rs.14,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
The contention taken up by the respondent No.2 that the petitioner / rider of the vehicle was under the influence of alcohol /intoxication stated and that has contributed for the accident.
The IO has also not invoked Sec.185 of MV Act.
Moreover during the course of cross-examination of RW.2 he has also categorically admitted that there are no documents produced that the rider of the vehicle was in intoxicated state.
Hence the contentions urged by the respondent No.2 does not hold any water in the eye of law.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner, he died during the pendency and respondent No.1(a) and (b) being the LR's of deceased respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Tractor - Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-44-TA-3025 and KA-44-TA- 3024 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
33. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,43,950/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/ RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
